business_problem: loveholidays needed to let product, design, and commercial teams test and ship ideas without waiting for scarce engineering and platform specialists, while also making infrastructure and data changes easier to self-serve safely.
solution_summary: loveholidays embedded Codex into both customer-experience prototyping and internal platform operations so more of the business could build software directly. Search Playground, built with the company's design system, frontend technologies, and Codex, lets non-engineers turn ideas into working travel experiences, gather feedback, and even launch them on the production site. Behind the scenes, the company encodes data-platform and infrastructure best practices, validations, and release checks into Codex-guided workflows so employees can propose changes, run validations, and move work through deployment without mastering every specialist tool. Codex has become a control plane across engineers and business users, so specialists spend less time handling routine requests and more time improving the platform. The result is an operating model where more experiments become products, deployments rise without more headcount, and data-platform efficiency improves along with cloud-cost discipline.

data_flow: Business ideas enter Search Playground through Codex, which uses loveholidays' design system and frontend stack to produce working experiences for feedback or launch. For infrastructure and data changes, users submit the intended change to Codex, which applies encoded best practices, runs checks, and guides work through release workflows.
business_outcome: loveholidays raised AI-assisted code changes from 7% to 79%, increased deployment frequency by 73% without more engineers, improved Data Platform change success from 58% to 93%, and lowered cloud-storage and processing costs while letting non-engineers ship new experiences.
